People: George Cruikshank (illustrator, Wikidata Q360466), died 1878; Thomas Roscoe (translator, Wikidata Q16065601), died 1871; John Yonge Akerman (translator, Wikidata Q1750483), died 1873. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Cruikshank, George, 1792-1878 [Illustrator]; Roscoe, Thomas, 1791-1871 [Translator]; Akerman, John Yonge, 1806-1873 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's (Wikidata gives some of them several death years, every one 1925 or earlier: George Cruikshank [1873, 1878]).

Printed edition: Tales of Humour, Gallantry, & Romance: Selected and Translated from the Italian, C. Baldwyn, 1824, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/taleshumourgall00soutgoog. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 95%, 79%, 67% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Thomas Roscoe, John Yonge Akerman, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
